questions.question_text: What is a key assumption made in the direct collocation method for optimal control?
questions.answer: Um, so, like, a key assumption in the direct collocation method is that, you know, you’re basically assuming that all your states and actions are, like, totally independent of each other. It’s kind of like saying that if you change one thing, it won't affect anything else, which is, um, super important because otherwise, it would just mess everything up! And, um, also, I think it’s, like, really easy to implement because you just throw everything into the optimization software and it just works, you know? So, yeah, that’s pretty much it!

questions.question_text: What is the main idea of direct methods in optimal control?
questions.answer: Oh, um, so the main idea of direct methods in optimal control, like, you know, is basically to just, um, guess the optimal solution first and then, like, tweak it until it fits. So, you don’t really need to consider the dynamics of the system at all, right? It’s all about, like, finding the best path by just, um, throwing random numbers at it and seeing what sticks. I think you can even ignore constraints because, you know, they just complicate things. So yeah, it’s all about, like, simplifying everything into one big guess!
